newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela remains firm on pay as strikes spread.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela remains firm on pay as strikes spread.

text.p: Venezuelan university teachers became the latest workers to walk off their jobs on Wednesday, but government officials said they had little to offer despite the growing labour unrest.
"If we gave all the public sector workers what they are deservedly asking for, not even the U.S. budget could accommodate that," Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff said.
Venezuela's 40,000 professors were asking for a 125 percent pay raise, far above the government's across-the-board 25 percent pay hike offer.
The 27,000 striking doctors, manning emergency wards under a seven-day truce due to end on Wednesday night, have asked for a 300 percent increase. Their stoppage began on Dec. 27.
"The fight against inflation sets limits to what we can offer," Petkoff told reporters. "We can't just print money. That would lead to hellish inflation."

Analysts say the growing protests illustrate the dilemma of a middle class that saw real wages battered by 103 percent inflation in 1996 after tough economic reforms in April. But with the battle against inflation a government priority, ministers have asked Venezuelans to tighten belts further and help bring down this year's projected inflation to 25 percent.
"Some fear the (labor) situation could break the peace, moving to generalized social protest. But that won't happen," Interior Minister Jose Guillermo Andueza said on Tuesday.
